definitionSource: User-supplied manuscript, Deployment Shifts and Measuring Robustness, November 5, 2026

definitions.L1: A policy is nominally competent at 0.5 times the shared standard nominal median. The method must preserve nominal competence without increasing nominal failure.
definitions.L2: Reliability improves over all severities on one side of an axis; mean return is noninferior over the entire nonnominal axis. L1 is also required.
definitions.L3: One fixed setting preserves axis-balanced full-suite return and improves unconditional suite reliability. L1 and L2 are also required.

criteria: L1 follows the author-requested qualitative nominal review, with borderline cases separate. L2 reuses saved one-sided tests; L3 uses the authoritative revised manuscript. Positive descriptive mean/AUC differences alone do not establish a level.
limitations: L1 is a post-hoc qualitative screen, not a 5% tolerance or statistical-equivalence test. The author requested this choice; explicit review annotations and nominal values are provided.
Saved L2 intervals use paired whole-policy bootstrap, 10000 resamples, seed 0; the mean-return margin is 5% of the absolute whole-axis reference mean. No new bootstrap was run.
The cached L2 analysis tests the selected setting per shift, not every setting on every shift. Unselected settings are not counted as failures.
TD3-TV Walker uses the inactive cap-500 comparator for its saved hierarchy tests, not ordinary standard TD3.
No adjustment for searching multiple settings/shifts is added; saved L2 evidence remains exploratory.
Manuscript-reported L1/L3 outcomes are labeled as reports, not independently revalidated. The author says to ignore OLD: Experiment Results and use the revised Results.
Supplied Pendulum names are confirmed, but algorithm and policy-seed identities are not. Archived custom TD3-KL cohorts remain opt-in.
